body_markdown:
If that[R125 Mustang](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/celebrate-125-years-with-the-ford-racing-r125-mustang/) isn’t quite your speed, maybe Ford’s other SEMA unveil will catch your interest—it certainly got ours. This 1985 bullnose F-250 may look modest for a SEMA build, but we think there’s some beauty to its restraint.


Ford Racing | Matt Johnson


The project is the brainchild of Matt Johnson, a mechanical engineer out of Klamath Falls, Oregon, who runs a small auto shop in the town. Like many of the trucks we find extra endearing, the story starts in a farm field, where Johnson discovered this pickup slumbering. He bought the depleted truck for $800 and intended to use it as a shop truck. Johnson has a history with these rigs and says he daily-drove one throughout college, as well as through other major milestones in his life.


Ford Racing | Matt Johnson


Ford Racing | Matt Johnson


Initially, he had no plans to pull off this sort of restomod—and certainly not with this truck. Johnson’s original idea, which put him in touch with Ford Racing Parts, was actually to install a 2.3-liter EcoBoost four-cylinder into an older[FJ40 Land Cruiser](https://www.hagerty.com/media/buying-and-selling/our-tame-fighter-pilot-goes-bombing-for-fjs-considers-pickling/) . After some discussions with the FRP team, however, the project shifted when Ford suggested that instead of the EcoBoost, he opt for one of Ford’s Heritage V-8s. Naturally, that sounded like a great idea—but suddenly the transplant candidate seemed inadequate.


Ford Racing | Matt Johnson


“To me, the little EcoBoost motor in the Land Cruiser is a perfect match,” says Johnson. “But a rowdy small-block, like the Heritage engine—that needs to go in a Ford. So, I said, ‘Let me just stop you right there on the Land Cruiser idea, because there’s a couple of cool Ford trucks I have behind the shop.'”


Ford Racing | Matt Johnson


That ranch hand[bullnose](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/hagerty-price-guide/its-time-to-appreciate-5-ford-trucks-under-50000/) was the perfect candidate. Of course, the engine is righteous—a Ford Racing 460-cubic-inch small-block making 575 horsepower and 575 lb-ft of torque. While many think of the Coyote 5.0-liter when they think of “new Ford V-8s,” that motor’s dual-overhead-cam design makes it a bit tricky to fit in certain applications. Because pushrod V-8s tend to have smaller footprints, Ford has recently recommitted to modernized tooling and assembly for these heritage engines.


Ford Racing | Matt Johnson


Ford Racing | Matt Johnson


Ford Racing | Matt Johnson


Other modifications include a re-engineered version of the truck’s Twin Traction-Beam (TTB) suspension courtesy of John Carrick at Carrick Customs, long-travel suspension, and a set of 37-inch Mickey Thompson Baja tires. Otherwise, the chassis and bodywork are all original, which makes this a more approachable build than much of what[SEMA](https://www.hagerty.com/media/tags/sema/) is known for. It’s incredibly tasteful, and we’re seriously digging this truck.
